- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; apply upward bias correction by 1–4%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1 to -1), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–3 days and smooth transition.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; forecast should converge toward 30-day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is volatile, reduce forecast slope to avoid overconfidence in trend continuation.
